disclosures.name: TestIssue59563TruncatedCoverPkgAll
disclosures.signature: go tool cover -func failed: exit status 2
disclosures.reason: The test shells out twice to the real toolchain, `go test -coverpkg=all -coverprofile=…` with cmd.Dir = testdata/issue59563 and then `go tool cover -func=…`, and expects a row for internal/coverage/cfile/testdata/issue59563/repro.go containing "large". The root cause is that the process's current directory does not sit under the GOROOT the process reports. On linux the test fails at emitdata_test.go:512, the `go tool cover -func` t.Fatalf: the converted host stages std's go.mod at <sandbox>/src and os/exec sets PWD to the sandbox path, so cmd/go reads the staged go.mod as an ordinary module named `std` and records the package as std/internal/...; cover -func's go list, run from the real GOROOT directory, refuses that path as not in std (exit status 2). A same-toolchain A/B differing only in run location shows both locations producing 10280 func rows with `repro.go:18: large 100.0%`, the only difference being the module-qualified `std/` prefix outside the reported GOROOT, so the coverage the test exists to check (issue 59563) is correct and only the rendering of the host's directory identity differs. The sandbox run-directory is deliberate (a test may write without touching the real tree), and GOROOT deliberately keeps pointing at the real installation, because repointing it at the mirrored ancestry regresses two validated packages that walk GOROOT: compress/gzip's issue14937 test and path/filepath (0 *.gz found against the real 4; 1 src/unicode entry against the real 19). go/build's TestLocalDirectory has the same root, where ImportDir finds no known root and answers ".". On windows the test passes on both sides. Retires if the host can place cwd under the reported GOROOT without repointing GOROOT at a junction view, or keep PWD from naming the sandbox.
disclosures.history:
RE-SIGNED AT go1.26.10 (2026-10-25, G; COORD ruled the re-sign, R diagnosed the linux path). The host-identity root below is unchanged, but its two paths now part by OS. LINUX takes emitdata_test.go:512, the `go tool cover -func` t.Fatalf: the ancestry view stages std's go.mod at <sandbox>/src, os/exec sets PWD to the sandbox path, so cmd/go records the package as std/internal/... and cover -func's go list, run from the real GOROOT directory, refuses it as not in std, exit status 2. WINDOWS no longer fails at all: G read the test at d804094d7a, Go pass / C# pass, and the go1.24.13 pin (signature "wanted 1 found, got 0", the :537 Errorf this record describes below) reported itself an ORPHAN there. So the windows scope retires and this entry is linux only; darwin joins only if its own re-read fails it. Retire plan (queued post-publish, COORD 2026-10-25): place cwd under the reported GOROOT, or keep PWD from naming the sandbox. THE go1.24.13 RECORD, kept as history: the assert requires the process's CURRENT DIRECTORY to sit under the GOROOT the process REPORTS. The test shells out twice to the real toolchain — `go test -coverpkg=all -coverprofile=…` with cmd.Dir = testdata/issue59563, then `go tool cover -func=…` — and scans the output for one row whose path has the prefix "internal/coverage/cfile/testdata/issue59563/repro.go" and contains "large".

BOTH subprocesses SUCCEED in the converted host and the full listing is produced; the divergence is one prefix. Measured A/B, same toolchain, same command, only the run location differing:

  control (real GOROOT/src/internal/coverage/cfile/testdata/issue59563)
    -> 10280 func rows; internal/coverage/cfile/testdata/issue59563/repro.go:18: large 100.0%
  experiment (identical layout — staged src/go.mod plus the ancestry path — OUTSIDE the reported GOROOT)
    -> 10280 func rows; std/internal/coverage/cfile/testdata/issue59563/repro.go:18: large 100.0%

Identical row count to the digit, identical functions, identical percentages. Outside the reported GOROOT the toolchain reads the staged src/go.mod as an ORDINARY module named `std` rather than as GOROOT's own standard library, so every package path becomes module-qualified; strings.HasPrefix then fails and nfound stays 0. The coverage the test exists to check is CORRECT — `large` is 100.0%, which is the whole point of issue 59563 — and only the rendering of the host's directory identity differs.

The sandbox run-directory is deliberate (a test may write without touching the real tree) and PackageAncestry deliberately keeps GOROOT pointing at the real installation, because repointing it at the junction-mirrored ancestry regresses two already-validated packages that WALK GOROOT: compress/gzip's issue14937 test and path/filepath (measured: 0 *.gz found against the real 4; 1 src/unicode entry against the real 19).

Same root as go/build's TestLocalDirectory, which the same cwd-vs-reported-GOROOT identity breaks in a different place: there ImportDir finds no known root and answers ".", where this one gets a module-qualified `std/` prefix. One cause, two manifestations.

Retires if the host can place cwd under the reported GOROOT without repointing GOROOT at a junction view, or if the toolchain's std-module identification stops depending on the directory's position.
